items.question_text: Two winches lift identical crates onto a lorry. Winch X takes 12 s and winch Y takes 30 s. Which winch has the greater power, and why?

options.a: Winch X, because it transfers the same energy in less time
options.b: Winch Y, because it works on the crate for longer
options.c: Neither, because both crates gain the same energy
options.d: Winch Y, because it is painted a brighter colour

feedback.b: Working for longer does not mean more power: the same energy in more time is less power.
feedback.c: They gain the same energy, but power is energy per second, so the faster winch has more power.
feedback.d: The colour of the winch has nothing to do with its power.

misconception_map.b: slip: thinks a longer time means a greater power

items.explanation: Both crates gain the same energy. Power = energy ÷ time, and X takes less time, so X has the greater power.

items.stem: A [[machine]] has a power of \([[P]]\,\text{W}\). How long does it take to transfer \([[E]]\,\text{J}\) of energy?

feedback.multiplied: This multiplies energy by power. Rearrange P = E ÷ t to \(t = \dfrac{E}{P} = \dfrac{[[E]]}{[[P]]}\).
feedback.upside-down: This divides the power by the energy. The time is energy ÷ power: \(t = \dfrac{[[E]]}{[[P]]}\).

sample_instances.question_text: A winch has a power of \(800\,\text{W}\). How long does it take to transfer \(4800\,\text{J}\) of energy?

wrong.misconception: This multiplies energy by power. Rearrange P = E ÷ t to \(t = \dfrac{E}{P} = \dfrac{4800}{800}\).
This divides the power by the energy. The time is energy ÷ power: \(t = \dfrac{4800}{800}\).

items.stem: A [[machine]] transfers \([[E]]\,\text{J}\) of energy in \([[t]]\,\text{s}\). Calculate its power.

feedback.multiplied: This multiplies energy by time. Power is the energy transferred each second: \(P = \dfrac{E}{t} = \dfrac{[[E]]}{[[t]]}\).
feedback.upside-down: This divides the time by the energy. Power = energy ÷ time: \(P = \dfrac{[[E]]}{[[t]]}\).

items.question_text: A toy car's motor transfers \(15\,000\,\text{J}\) of energy in \(30\,\text{s}\). Calculate its power.

wrong.misconception: This multiplies energy by time. Power = energy ÷ time: \(15\,000 \div 30 = 500\,\text{W}\).
This divides time by energy. Power = energy ÷ time: \(15\,000 \div 30 = 500\,\text{W}\).
